gpt.text:
Given this handoff, you’re in a clean state: there’s a current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`), no PASS candidates waiting, and nothing currently marked INCONCLUSIVE. The “Next Commands” block is the intended runbook.

### What each command will do (and why this order makes sense)

1) **AUB autopilot (module-level tuning)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
- Runs module experiments from `module_registry.yaml`.
- `--select-best` typically promotes the best-performing module configuration into the current working baseline (depending on how your tool writes artifacts).
- This is usually first because it can improve component performance before you try system-level combinations.

2) **System autopilot (system candidate search)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
- Tries system-level candidate configurations (e.g., different combinations of modules/settings) defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.
- Run this after module tuning so it’s exploring with the best available components.

3) **Generate “next fix” recommendations**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
- Produces a markdown report suggesting the next most promising fixes/experiments based on results to date.
- Best run after the above so the report reflects the latest outcomes.

### Practical execution notes
- Run from repo root so relative paths resolve.
- If you have any notion of “locked” champion artifacts, consider copying `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` aside before running, in case `--select-best` updates references.
- After step (1) and (2), check the newly written reports/logs for: selected winner, any regressions, and whether any trials were marked INCONCLUSIVE.

If you paste the stdout/stderr (or the generated report paths) after running command (1), I can help interpret whether the selected-best outcome is actually safe to promote vs. needing a rerun or constraints adjustment.
